text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Transformer maker Smit Trafo to close loss-making U.S. plant in Charleston. (p1)
- Rumours about possible joint-venture between KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and Swissair heat up again. (p1)
- KPN unit PTT Telecom and rival Libertel not allowed to bid for two new mobile telecom licences. (p1)
- Loss-making transhipment company European Bulk Services to slash 280 of 651 jobs as part of new restructuring. (p3)
- Retailer Groenewoudt Groep takes over Belgium's perfumery chain Iri Paris XL with 58 shops. (p4)
- Chemical firm Akzo Nobel's shares jump six guilders to Dfl 198.60 on positive test results of new anti-depression medicine. (p9)
VOLKSKRANT
- Coalition under pressure as Liberal leader Frits Bolkestein refuses to return from holidays to explain conduct as supervisory board member of Merck Sharp & Dohme. (p19)
- Uncertainty grows over outcome of talks on attempt by South Korea's Samsung to take over bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p2)
- Charter carriers say Schiphol airport discriminates against departing passengers, charging them five times more than those who change planes. (p2)
- Akzo Nobel and unions closer to agreement on moving part of production from Ede to Poland. (p19)
DE TELEGRAAF
- KLM subsidiary Transavia economises in bid to ward off pending losses. (p1)
- KLM and partner Northwest Airlines bring cooperation up for discussion again. (p25)
- Fiscal fraud in cross-border transactions growing again, says junior finance minister Wim Vermeend. (p25)
- Philips Electronics' new president Cor Boonstra wants to conquer Japan's consumer market. (p25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Software company Baan to cooperate with Sun Microsystems. (p11)
- Strong growth of temp workers in metal industry. (p11)
TROUW
- Bank insurer ING and Chinese partners start building houses in Beijing, China. (p6)
